paragraphs: Modified Rule of Four (for river play with 10+ outs)
Example for a combo draw with 15 outs (15)(3) + 9 = odds of improving 45 + 9 = odds of improving 54% = odds of improving.
This formula has a maximum absolute error of less than 1% for up to 19 outs. So now you have a great system to quickly double-check your odds of improving. Use this technique in every hand you play.

There are 2,162 turn and river permutations on any given flop. If the order that the turn and river are dealt doesn’t matter, there are really only 1,081 permutations. It’s pretty easy to figure this out. By the time the flop is dealt, your two hole cards and the three cards on the flop are visible.

If you subtract the five visible cards from a deck of 52 cards, you realize that there are 47 unseen cards. One of those cards has to be dealt on the turn. After the turn is dealt, one of the remaining 46 cards must be dealt on the river. 47 x 46 = 2,162. If the order of these cards doesn’t matter, you just divide by two to find the total number of turn and river permutations. 2,162/2 = 1,081.

Below is a list of backdoor draws and the equities associated with them. These percentages my seem small, but they can have a tremendously profitable impact on your global strategy if implemented correctly. Thus, they are included in this section.
